_comment: Brokers TradeZulu knows about.
Two jobs. It tells the web interface which brokers to offer and which trade
servers each one has, so nobody has to remember whether their server is
called VantageMarkets-Live or VantageInternational-Live. And it tells the
provisioner which MetaTrader build to install, which the user never sees.
label      what the account form shows
servers    the trade servers to offer. An empty list means the form asks
the user to type one, which is always allowed anyway -- brokers
add servers without telling anyone.
installer  the MetaTrader build to use. Where a broker ships its own, use
it: the generic MetaQuotes terminal cannot resolve a name like
VantageMarkets-Live at all and offers to open a new account
instead, which looks exactly like a rejected password.
matches    substrings that identify this broker from a server name, used
to pick the template. The server name is what decides, because
it always arrives correct -- it comes from the broker.
A broker with no installer of its own runs on the generic build, which
connects to most brokers by name. Adding one is a label, its servers, and
a matches entry.
MetaQuotes hosts a build per broker at a predictable address, which is why
those are preferred over a broker's own download page: the pages move, wrap
the file in a landing page, or hand out a different build per region.
